Few companies sit closer to the race to power AI data centers than Bloom Energy (NYSE:BE). Bloom Energy shares have climbed 157% year to date (YTD) to $223.03, a run that leaves rival fuel cell stocks and the hydrogen sector well behind. The fuel cell maker has become a key supplier of on-site power for AI data center operators that can't wait on grid connections.

gchutka / E+ via Getty Images

Not long ago, Oracle (NYSE:ORCL) confirmed Bloom Energy as the primary power source for Project Jupiter, its AI data center campus in New Mexico. Installation of Bloom Energy fuel cells is already underway at the site. That confirmation arrives before Q3 2026 results, scheduled for next week.

Data Center Exposure Splits the Fuel Cell Group

Meanwhile, FuelCell Energy (NASDAQ:FCEL) stock is up 77% YTD to $12.91, a strong gain that still sits well behind Bloom Energy shares. FuelCell manufactures utility-scale fuel cell platforms and earns revenue as modules are ordered, built and serviced.

Plug Power (NASDAQ:PLUG) stock is down 30% YTD to $1.38, moving in the opposite direction from Bloom Energy shares. Weighted toward hydrogen fuel and handling equipment, Plug Power's business has little tied to stationary power for computing.

title: Does The Move In Snowflake Stock Change Anything?
detail:
Does The Move In Snowflake Stock Change Anything?
Trefis Team

Image from Pexels

Snowflake (SNOW) stock rose 59.3% from January 18 to October 15, 2026, against 12.5% for the S&P 500. The company reported quarterly results three times along the way, on February 25, May 27 and September 2. Buyers appear to be betting that customers using AI on Snowflake's data platform will keep its sales growth climbing while its losses shrink. So how much faster is Snowflake growing than it was in January?

Snowflake Has Grown Faster Every Quarter Since January

Snowflake's revenue is growing about five percentage points faster than when the rise began. Revenue grew 30.1% from a year earlier in fiscal Q4 2026, the quarter that ended January 31. That pace reached 35.1% in fiscal Q2 2027, with growth registering higher in each quarter along the way. Product revenue, nearly all of Snowflake's sales, grew 37% in that latest quarter. On the September 2 call, management said customers using AI on Snowflake consume more across the data platform.

The stock's two largest one-day gains during the rise came right after the May 27 and September 2 reports. Shares rose 37% on May 28, the day after Snowflake reported fiscal Q1 2027 results. On the September 2 call, management said it had raised its fiscal 2027 forecast for product revenue growth by more than five percentage points, to 36%. The stock gained 16.6% the next day.

A run higher can leave Snowflake a larger share of what you own than you planned. See how to protect a concentrated position.

How Far Have Snowflake's Losses Shrunk?

Snowflake's operating loss came to 17.0% of revenue in fiscal Q2 2027, against 29.7% in fiscal Q2 2026. The company's losses are narrowing, though it still loses money. Management said on the September 2 call that Snowflake remains on track for a profit under standard accounting rules (GAAP) in fiscal Q4 2028.

Yet management also said its fast-growing AI workloads carry a lower margin today. So Snowflake keeps less of each dollar on the sales that are lifting its growth, at least for now.

Why Snowflake Is Still Valued On Its Sales

Snowflake is still valued on its sales because it remains unprofitable, despite the faster growth. It lost $1.09 billion over the twelve months to July 31, 2026, so its price-to-earnings multiple is not meaningful. Its operating loss over those twelve months stood at 22.8% of revenue. That marks the smallest figure at any quarter end from fiscal Q2 2021 on, yet it is still a loss.

On sales, the stock trades at 21.5 times, against 3.1 for the S&P 500. At that multiple, the share price appears to assume that both the faster growth and the shrinking losses continue.

title: What Is The Biggest Threat To Microsoft Stock?
detail:
What Is The Biggest Threat To Microsoft Stock?
Trefis Team

Explore stocks on Coinbase

Microsoft Is Spending Heavily To Meet AI Demand

The cost is the AI capacity Microsoft is building, and the company's executives raised it on that same call. Customer demand still exceeds the capacity Microsoft has available, management said. In July, the company expected to spend over $50 billion on capital in fiscal Q1 2027, covering the July to September quarter. This figure includes the effect of a change in how it counts some leases. Microsoft also expects capital spending for fiscal 2027 as a whole to grow from the year before.

That heavy spending already shows in Microsoft's financial results. Gross margin was 67.2% in fiscal Q4 2026, against 68.6% a year earlier. Management attributed this decline to a shift in sales toward Azure and to continued investment in AI infrastructure. Free cash flow, the cash left after that spending, fell to $19.6 billion from $25.6 billion a year earlier, even as cash from operations rose.

Microsoft's Cloud Business And The Price You Pay

Microsoft's Intelligent Cloud segment brought in $39.3 billion in fiscal Q4 2026. This accounted for more than two-fifths of the company's revenue and represented 32% growth from a year earlier. No other Microsoft segment grew as fast during that quarter, and revenue in Azure and other cloud services grew 43%. Microsoft is building capacity to keep up with precisely this growth.

At today's price, there is little room for that spending to disappoint. Microsoft stock trades at 30.0 times its earnings over the past twelve months, against 22.7 for the S&P 500. At the end of June, the same earnings were priced at 20.7 times, the lowest at any quarter end since fiscal 2017. On October 15, the shares closed less than 1% below their highest close of the past year. The current stock price appears to assume the spending will pay off.

How Serious Is The Spending Risk For Microsoft?

Microsoft shareholders face a real but slow risk. Operating margin was 45.1% in fiscal Q4 2026, against 44.9% a year earlier, meaning Microsoft still keeps a slightly larger share of its sales as operating profit. For fiscal 2027 as a whole, management expects operating margin to be down less than 1 point, even as the company invests to meet growing demand.

So far, the cost shows up in Microsoft's cash and its gross margin, while operating margin has held steady. Free cash flow is the key metric to watch in Microsoft's next report, which will cover the July to September quarter.

A $1,000 investment in Oracle (NYSE: ORCL) could grow to roughly $2,430 by 2029. This assumes that the company converts its cloud backlog on the schedule management has outlined, it meets Wall Street's fiscal 2029 average per-share earnings estimate of $15.80, and the stock continues to trade at a recent 20 price-to-earnings (P/E) multiple.

Oracle's remaining performance obligations (RPO) stood at $664 billion as of fiscal first-quarter 2027 ended Aug. 31. That's an increase of $209 billion from a year earlier.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Delays in bringing more cloud capacity online are a risk that could throw off Wall Street's estimates. Still, Oracle's RPO is contracted revenue, providing line of sight into future revenue at a time when demand for AI infrastructure continues to outpace available capacity across the industry.

Image source: Getty Images.
Oracle expects half the backlog to convert to revenue in the next 36 months

Oracle provides cloud infrastructure services for artificial intelligence (AI) workloads, Fusion applications that run core business processes, and the Oracle Database. This combination of infrastructure, applications, and AI solutions differentiates Oracle from competitors and continues to drive strong demand from enterprises.

Cloud infrastructure revenue reached $7.4 billion in the first quarter of fiscal 2027, up 121% year over year. RPO rose $26 billion from the prior quarter, and management expects roughly half of the total backlog to convert into sales during the next 36 months.

Company projections for the full fiscal year call for total revenue of at least $90 billion and non-GAAP (meaning not in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles) earnings per share of $8.10. Demand is not letting up. Graphics processing unit (GPU) utilization stood at 97.9% in the quarter, reflecting that nearly every chip is being used by customers for AI workloads, and capacity that came up for renewal was renewed or resold at a 20% premium to prior contracts.

Synergy Research Group has reported that generative AI-specific cloud services grew 165% year over year in recent periods, with Oracle among the fastest-growing providers outside the top three (Amazon, Microsoft, and Alphabet's Google). Goldman Sachs projects that the five largest U.S. hyperscalers, including Oracle, will spend about $1.2 trillion on AI infrastructure in 2027.

Borrowed money is paying for a growing share of the AI expansion, and credit investors have started to reprice the risk. On the Charles Schwab On Investing episode "Who's Financing the AI Boom?," Bryan Whalen described how large the shift has become.

"Last year in 2025, net issuance in the investment grade corporate bond market was about half a trillion dollars. This year it's expected to double. And almost the entirety of that doubling has been in the AI data center required capital spend," Whalen said. The portfolio manager also said that the cash buffer is gone: "Three years ago, these hyperscalers had over $250 billion of free cash flow collectively. This year they're negative."

24/7 Wall St.
Cash Flow Gaps Now Show Up in the Filings

Company results support his point. Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META) generated $784 million of second-quarter free cash flow, down from $8.55 billion a year earlier. Over the same quarter, capex reached $30.12 billion and long-term debt rose to $83.66 billion. Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) reported trailing free cash flow of negative $7.6 billion. Oracle (NYSE:ORCL) posted free cash flow of negative $5.4 billion on $28.5 billion of capex and completed a $20 billion at-the-market equity program.
